awd_titl_txt: Travel: NSF Student Travel Grant for 2025 ACM SIGCOMM Internet Measurement Conference (IMC)
awd_abstract_narration:
This project seeks to fund US-based students to attend ACM SIGCOMM Internet Measurement Conference (IMC) 2025, held in Madison, Wisconsin on October 28 - 31, 2025.  ICM 2025 is a premier annual forum that attracts high-quality, forward-looking research contributions and provides a vibrant forum for technical and professional exchanges.  ICM 2025 will expose students to cutting-edge developments in the field and enable interactions with world-leading researchers. Students will gain feedback on their ongoing work, broaden their academic perspectives, and build lasting professional connections. 

This project supports students from US universities to attend ACM IMC 2025 conference in person. Students will have the opportunity to present their work and be exposed to state-of-the-art developments in the field. They will also have the opportunity to interact with peers from institutions worldwide, meet with senior researchers, and participate in discussions that are likely to shape the future of the field.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This project supported graduate student participation in the 25th ACM Internet Measurement Conference (IMC 2025), held in Madison, Wisconsin, from October 28-31, 2025. IMC is a leading international conference focused on measuring, analyzing, and understanding the Internet. Research presented at the conference helps improve knowledge of how Internet infrastructure operates, how it changes over time, and how its performance, reliability, and security can be improved.

The award provided travel support to students from U.S. institutions who otherwise might have had limited resources to attend the conference. A total of 15 students were selected from universities across the United States, including Northwestern University, Northeastern University, the University of Southern California, Georgia Institute of Technology, Johns Hopkins University, Virginia Tech, Duke University, the University of Oregon, and the University of California San Diego. The NSF-supported portion of the travel program provided $15,000 in total support.

The project contributed to the intellectual merit of the Internet measurement research community by enabling students to engage directly with current research and researchers in the field. Students attended technical presentations and workshops, discussed emerging research ideas, received feedback on ongoing work, and learned about new methods for studying Internet infrastructure and behavior. These interactions help students improve their research and develop new ideas and collaborations.

The broader impacts of the project centered on expanding access to professional development and research opportunities for the next generation of computing and networking researchers. Students participated in poster sessions, workshops, and mentoring activities that provided opportunities to interact with established researchers and peers, discuss career paths, and build professional networks. In selecting awardees, the travel grant program sought broad representation across institutions, geographic regions, and academic levels.
